headline: High: OpenBBTerminal can expose financial data to Prefect’s broad egress and shared orchestration paths, creating leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and multiple API surfaces, so if Prefect passes OpenBB outputs through shared files or messages, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions. Prefect’s orchestration role makes that bridge plausible, but no direct documented shared channel is provided, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests OpenBBTerminal output from a shared workspace, queue, or message payload without sanitization
IF OpenBBTerminal content is routed through MCP or API responses that Prefect later parses as instructions
mitigations: Disable any shared file or message bridge between the agents
Add strict schema validation for all OpenBBTerminal outputs before Prefect consumes them
Prefix/sandbox all tool outputs as data, not instructions
Review one end-to-end sample payload for prompt-like text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every inter-agent message

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while Prefect has broad network egress. If Prefect receives OpenBBTerminal context or files, it can transmit sensitive material off-host. That combination is dangerous by default in a pairwise workflow, and the lack of explicit isolation or retention controls pushes severity to high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs financial or licensed data into a workspace Prefect can read
IF Prefect forwards task context or file contents to external services during orchestration
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Block Prefect from reading OpenBBTerminal files
Redact financial and licensed fields before handoff
Verify outbound destinations for Prefect tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability, while Prefect’s profile exposes only broad egress and a GitHub API read surface. The pair therefore lacks a strong shared-write conflict path. Any conflict would require unusual external coordination not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable directory
IF Prefect is configured with additional write scopes not shown in its profile
mitigations: Keep shared resources read-only
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents
Confirm Prefect has no hidden write scopes
Use separate git working trees
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can generate financial outputs that Prefect may treat as workflow metadata or downstream inputs. Because Prefect is an orchestrator, a mistaken assumption that OpenBBTerminal output is authoritative can cascade into automated actions. The interaction is plausible in default orchestration patterns, so high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect uses OpenBBTerminal output as a task parameter or decision input without verification
IF downstream Prefect flows act on OpenBBTerminal-generated facts automatically
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any actioning flow
Require validation against a second source
Mark OpenBBTerminal output as untrusted in Prefect
Log and diff all derived values before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, but Prefect’s profile only shows workflow metadata and broad egress, with no residency or retention controls documented. The mismatch is therefore a compliance risk if regulated data is handed to Prefect, though the evidence does not prove a specific violation. Uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is routed from OpenBBTerminal into Prefect-managed workflows
IF Prefect retains or transmits that data beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Prefect workflows
Document retention and residency expectations
Strip identifiers before orchestration
Review vendor terms for both tools
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
